measured_snapshot: Frozen committed engine/wrapper/NodeJS compiler from codex/puzzlejax-gpu-throughput; benchmark source hashes recorded in each result.
builds: Reused hash-verified baseline-fixed and optimized-fixed extension builds. Both contain the byte-backed batched flag fix; only packed-cell scoring/win checks and cached target lists differ.
regression: 16 level-zero games at batch 1/thread 1 and batch 64/threads 8, plus level 1 of Sokoban Basic, Zen, Sokoban Match 3 and Microban at batch 64/threads 8. Two seeds, 300 steps, nine alternating trials, exact complete-output hashes. Action generation and reset excluded from A/B timing.
cpu_curve: Core i9-9980XE, affinity 0-31, min(batch,32) threads. Random actions, full RL outputs and win counting included in timing. Reset before each trial excluded. Two warmups, five seeded trials. Median/IQR without selecting thread counts or fastest samples.
cpu_topology: 18 physical cores, 36 logical CPUs. Affinity 0-31 spans all 18 physical cores and 14 additional SMT siblings.
extension: Initial stopping floor 64 was increased to 1024 because small-batch dips stopped several curves prematurely. Preserved timings have per-point driver hashes; extension_history retains the initial configuration. Only the driver/stopping limits changed; worker, wrapper, library and rollout protocol stayed identical. Initial driver is archived under provenance/.
pilot: A preliminary 16-thread curve was stopped and excluded from the figure. Published measurements use up to 32 threads, matching the archived C++ resource ceiling.
comparability: JAX H200 timings are reused without changes: final-carry output, continuing rollouts. C++ returns full RL outputs and resets between trials. NodeJS curves retain historical statistics. Use paired regression data, not historical-curve ratios, to estimate optimization gains.
workspace_isolation: Shared research edits, shared C++ extension and dirty NodeJS/JAX engine files were not modified. Work committed from an isolated worktree.
build_source_check: All optimized C++ source hashes match the recorded build except a single comment in bindings.cpp describing byte-backed flags. Replacing that comment with its pre-commit text reproduces the recorded hash exactly; executable code is identical.
